title: What's behind today's income shock? A YieldMax Nvidia fund is down 27%in 30 days. Are covered-call funds as safe as they sound?
author: tickeron_community
selftext:
Income funds aren't safe from the chip selloff: YieldMax's NVDA  
distribution fund is down 27% in 30 days. Elsewhere, SCHD faces QYLD,  
PFF faces SCHD, and two AAA CLO funds square off. Plus buffer ETFs and  
a $115 objective for MUB. Today's overview of the income and hedging  
ideas is below. Which one would you actually hold?  
  
Here is the rundown, drawn from today's write-ups.  
  
\*\*1. NVIT\*\* — NVIT declined roughly 27.3% over the last 30 days,  
sliding from about $48.71 in mid-October to approximately $35.42 by  
mid-November 2026.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/yieldmax-nvda-performance-distribution-target-25-etf-nvit-slides-27-3-over-30-days-39655/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/yieldmax-nvda-performance-distribution-target-25-etf-nvit-slides-27-3-over-30-days-39655/)  
  
\*\*2. SCHD vs QYLD\*\* — Weighing Dividend Growth Against High-Yield  
Covered Calls in 2026. Two setups, one head-to-head. Which one comes  
out ahead? The breakdown is in the link.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/schd-vs-qyld-weighing-dividend-growth-against-high-yield-covered-calls-in-2026-39719/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/schd-vs-qyld-weighing-dividend-growth-against-high-yield-covered-calls-in-2026-39719/)  
  
\*\*3. SOXY\*\* — SOXY is the YieldMax Target 12 Semiconductor Option  
Income ETF, an actively managed fund that pursues a 12% annual income  
target plus capital appreciation by selling options on a concentrated  
basket of semiconductor stocks. Target, not a promise.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/soxy-s-path-to-56-gains-weighing-the-yieldmax-semiconductor-etf-s-120-target-39703/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/soxy-s-path-to-56-gains-weighing-the-yieldmax-semiconductor-etf-s-120-target-39703/)  
  
\*\*4. iShares National Muni Bond ETF (MUB)\*\* — Because MUB is an ETF,  
it does not carry the individual analyst price targets that stocks  
receive; the $115 objective discussed here is a technical and  
round-number level drawn from public market commentary, not an analyst  
consensus.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/ishares-national-muni-bond-etf-mub-eyes-move-toward-115-10-potential-39491/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/ishares-national-muni-bond-etf-mub-eyes-move-toward-115-10-potential-39491/)  
  
\*\*5. XLSI\*\* — The central target of $26.50 is a technical objective,  
not an analyst-derived target; no Wall Street analysts publish price  
targets for this ETF. With the fund trading near $23.90, reaching  
$26.50 would require roughly an 11% advance — a substantial move for a  
covered-call fund. Target, not a promise.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/state-street-consumer-staples-select-sector-spdr-premium-income-etf-xlsi-eyes-11-move-to-26-50-39455/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/state-street-consumer-staples-select-sector-spdr-premium-income-etf-xlsi-eyes-11-move-to-26-50-39455/)  
  
\*\*6. PFF vs SCHD\*\* — Weighing Preferred Income Against Quality  
Dividend Growth. Two setups, one head-to-head. Which one comes out  
ahead? The breakdown is in the link.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/pff-vs-schd-weighing-preferred-income-against-quality-dividend-growth-39716/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/pff-vs-schd-weighing-preferred-income-against-quality-dividend-growth-39716/)  
  
\*\*7. CLOX vs JAAA\*\* — Weighing Two AAA CLO ETFs for Floating-Rate  
Income. Two setups, one head-to-head. Which one comes out ahead? The  
breakdown is in the link.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/clox-vs-jaaa-weighing-two-aaa-clo-etfs-for-floating-rate-income-39547/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/clox-vs-jaaa-weighing-two-aaa-clo-etfs-for-floating-rate-income-39547/)  
  
\*\*8. BALI vs ISPY\*\* — Weighing Two Routes to Large-Cap Equity Income.  
Two setups, one head-to-head. Which one comes out ahead? The breakdown  
is in the link.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/bali-vs-ispy-weighing-two-routes-to-large-cap-equity-income-39744/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/bali-vs-ispy-weighing-two-routes-to-large-cap-equity-income-39744/)  
  
\*\*9. SPYT vs YMAX\*\* — Weighing Two Distinct Paths to Option-Income  
Yield. Two setups, one head-to-head. Which one comes out ahead? The  
breakdown is in the link.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/spyt-vs-ymax-weighing-two-distinct-paths-to-option-income-yield-39549/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/spyt-vs-ymax-weighing-two-distinct-paths-to-option-income-yield-39549/)  
  
\*\*10. BUFB\*\* — Exploring Innovator's Laddered Buffer ETF for Equity  
Exposure. Business model, catalysts and risks inside.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/bufb-exploring-innovator-s-laddered-buffer-etf-for-equity-exposure-39691/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/bufb-exploring-innovator-s-laddered-buffer-etf-for-equity-exposure-39691/)  
  
\*\*11. JAJL\*\* — JAJL is an actively managed "defined outcome"  
exchange-traded fund (ETF) issued by Innovator Capital Management. The  
fund seeks to track the price return of the S&P 500 through the SPDR  
S&P 500 ETF Trust, up to a cap, while buffering 100% of downside  
losses over each six-month outcome period, before fees and expenses.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/jajl-etf-defined-outcome-approach-to-s-p-500-exposure-with-built-in-buffer-39692/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/jajl-etf-defined-outcome-approach-to-s-p-500-exposure-with-built-in-buffer-39692/)  
  
Would you actually hold a covered-call or income fund after a 27%  
slide like this?  
  
Not financial advice. Figures are from today's (Nov 17) write-ups,  
using intraday or latest-close prices, not live quotes. Price targets  
are targets, not promises.
